questions.question: Which are the two social groups in India which are most vulnerable to poverty?

options.text: Scheduled tribes and Other Backward Classes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Scheduled tribes and Scheduled castes.**__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• The social groups most vulnerable to poverty are the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribe households.
 
• Both of these groups have above-average levels of poverty indicators in the rural and the urban population.
 
• 51 out of 100 people belonging to scheduled tribes are not able to meet their basic needs.
 
• Similarly, 50% of casual workers in urban areas are below the poverty line.
 
• About 50% of landless agricultural workers and 43% of scheduled castes are also poor. 
 
• Women, elderly people, and female infants are the poorest of the poor because they are denied equal access to resources available to the family.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

__
 
• Several provisions have been incorporated in the Constitution for safeguarding and promoting the interests and rights of the Scheduled Tribes.
 
• Article 46
 
 
• The state shall promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker section
 
• Protect them from social injustice and all forms of exploitation.
 
 
 
• Article 23
 
 
• Prohibits traffic in human beings, beggars, forced labor has a special significance for Scheduled Tribes.
 
 
 
• Article 243D provides reservation of Seats for Scheduled Tribes in Panchayats. 
 
• Article 330 provides reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the House of the People.
 
• Article 332 provides reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in Legislative Assemblies of the States.
 
• Article 334 provides the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and the State Vidhan Sabha

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__ **

 
• ** Forward castes** and Brahmins are generally considered to be among the most privileged and affluent social groups in India. While there may be individual cases of poverty within these groups, they do not face the same systemic barriers and discrimination as Scheduled tribes and Scheduled castes.
 
• **Scheduled tribes and Other Backward Classes (OBCs)** are both marginalized social groups in India. However, OBCs are generally considered to be less vulnerable to poverty than Scheduled tribes, as they have greater access to education and employment opportunities.
 
• **Brahmins are traditionally considered to be a high-caste social group**, while Scheduled castes are traditionally considered to be a low-caste social group. While poverty rates may be higher among Scheduled castes, Brahmins as a group do not face the same systemic barriers and discrimination as Scheduled castes.

questions.question: ‘Ships’ is related to ‘Fleet’ in the same way as ‘Ants’ is related to ‘________’.
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Collective Nouns → a count noun that denotes a group of individuals.

__
 
• ‘Ships’ is related to ‘Fleet’ → A group of **ships** sailing together, engaged in the same activity, or under the same ownership is called **Fleet**.

Similarly, 

 
• ‘Ants’ is related to ‘________’ → A group of **ants** is called a **colony**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

**Gaggle: **

This term is primarily used to describe a group of geese that are not in flight; when in flight, they are often referred to as a skein, team, or wedge. Therefore, 'Gaggle' does not relate to ants and is not the correct analogy.

**Herd: **

This term is typically used to refer to a group of large animals, especially hoofed mammals, such as cows, elephants, or deer. Since ants do not fit the category of large animals or the behavior associated with herding, 'Herd' is not the correct analogy for a group of ants.

**Shoal:**

A shoal refers to a group of fish that swim together. Shoals are usually composed of fish of the same species, and the gathering can serve purposes such as social reasons, protection, and efficient foraging. While 'Shoal' suggests a governed, cohesive movement similar to a fleet in water, it is specifically used for fish and not ants, making it incorrect in this analogy.

Hence, '**Colony**' is the correct answer.
